commits.edited_message:
Composite the alpha of a luma-only image directly on its Y plane

Op_flatten_alpha_plane converts its input to planar RGB, composites the
alpha plane onto the colour planes, and converts back to the source
colorspace. There is no operator from RGB back to a luma-only image, so
compositing a monochrome image with alpha failed with "unsupported color
conversion" for monochrome and RGB targets (the planner flattens first
because that is the cheapest way to drop the alpha plane) and only worked
for a YCbCr target, where the planner converts before it flattens. This
predates the per-plane ColorState.

A luma-only image (colorspace monochrome, or YCbCr with chroma
monochrome) is now composited directly on its Y plane against the BT.601
luma of the background colour, which is exact for the grey backgrounds
this feature is used with. The per-plane composite loop is shared between
the luma and the RGB path, and an alpha plane that is no deeper than the
colour planes is weighted at its own depth. Direct callers get errors
instead of undefined behaviour when no composition mode is set, the image
has no alpha plane, the depths are incompatible with the Pixel type, or
the alpha plane has a different size. Bayer images are declined at plan
time.

Tests: monochrome to monochrome at 8 and 10 bits with exact values,
monochrome to interleaved RGB, a checkerboard, and a coloured background
that checks the BT.601 weighting.

coupling: The first edited commit narrows the storage-width invariant in Op_flatten_alpha_plane's planner from all planes to the colour planes. On its own this is safe: the unchanged later bit-depth guard still requires the alpha depth to equal the common colour depth, so an alpha plane with a different storage width cannot be planned. The second edited commit then permits an alpha plane that is no deeper than the colour planes at both plan time and conversion time. On its own that is also safe: the unchanged all-plane storage-width guard still rejects an 8-bit alpha plane when 16-bit colour planes select the uint16_t compositing instance. Only their composition lets a standards-conformant uncompressed monochrome image with a 16-bit Y plane and an 8-bit alpha plane reach composite_plane<uint16_t>. That path casts the one-byte alpha plane to uint16_t samples, halves its byte stride, and reads two bytes per sample past the end of the alpha allocation. The PoC builds the file entirely through public HEIF boxes and reaches the fault with heif_context_read_from_memory_without_copy() and heif_decode_image(). A correct fix has to restore a cross-plane invariant consistently for the planner and the direct conversion path while retaining the intended no-deeper-alpha behavior; changing only one commit's local relaxation leaves the other edited invariant inconsistent with the pointer type used by the shared composite loop.
